You are a code worker editing the freytag-forge repo. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge; edit files here directly and ONLY the files you own. Never edit /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge itself. Do NOT git commit and do NOT touch .git. No network calls, no billed runs, no Playwright browser runs, never call the OpenAI API.

OWNED FILES (all new): frontend/e2e/authored-spans.js, frontend/e2e/authored-spans.test.js, frontend/e2e/attribution-audit.js, frontend/e2e/attribution-audit.test.js. Nothing else.

WHY: The hosted canon judge needs to know which SENTENCES of a turn were inserted by the game runtime from authored package text, instead of a whole-turn marker (a marker says the turn contains authored text, not which text, and so can excuse unrelated narrator leaks on the same turn). The runtime composes a turn from narrator prose plus separate authored segments: a committed reveal's `delivery_text` (knowledge.yaml entry for each id in the bundle's selected_reveal.knowledge_ids), a cue's `cue_text` (handoffs.yaml; bundle cue_stage.fact_id when delivered), a handoff `fallback_text` (handoffs.yaml; replaces the narrator prose when the narrator missed required terms; see storygame/runtime/engine.py near `_missing_handoff_terms` and `delivery.fallback_text`), a transition's `bridge_text` (plot.md YAML front matter per scene, keyed by transition id, e.g. t_3b_3c; see engine.py `_apply_authored_transition` and the pacing.yaml `transitions:` list giving source_scene_id/target_scene_id per id), the target scene's `entry_text` (plot.md front matter), and ending route text (storylet-routes.yaml `fallback_text`, appended by the engine's ending backstop near engine.py line 509). READ those engine functions and the package files first so your eligibility rules mirror what the engine can actually append on a turn; do not guess. Attempt bundle shape: storygame/runtime/attempt_bundle.py (outcome, transition_cause, story_complete, selected_reveal{knowledge_ids, delivery_fact_ids}, cue_stage{fact_id, delivered, consumed}, committed_delta{fact_predicates, scene_from, scene_to}, pre_state.scene_id).

API to export from frontend/e2e/authored-spans.js (other tasks will import exactly these names):
1. `loadAuthoredText(root = <repo root>)` -> an object with Maps/arrays: knowledge delivery texts by id; cue texts and handoff fallback texts by fact_id; bridge texts by transition id plus a map from `${source}>${target}` to the bridge text via pacing.yaml transitions; entry texts by scene id; route fallback texts with whatever fact/event ids the YAML gives. Use the `yaml` package already used in frontend/e2e (see package-clock.js and roleplay-judge.js) and parse plot.md front matter yourself (the block between the first two `---` lines of each scene section; look at how plot.md is laid out and how storygame/story_package/ loads it; handle that the file has several front-matter blocks). No regex-based parsing of free prose; structural parsing only.
2. `eligibleAuthoredTexts(bundle, authored)` -> array of {text, source:{kind:'delivery'|'cue'|'handoff_fallback'|'bridge'|'entry'|'route_fallback', id}}: ONLY for bundles whose outcome is 'committed', and ONLY texts this turn could legitimately contain: deliveries for selected_reveal.knowledge_ids; the cue for cue_stage.fact_id when delivered; handoff fallback texts for selected_reveal.delivery_fact_ids / staged handoff facts you can identify from the bundle (pre_state.staged_handoff_fact_ids); the bridge for scene_from->scene_to and the entry text of scene_to when committed_delta.scene_from differs from scene_to (or transition_cause is not 'none'); route fallback texts only when story_complete is true or the route's fact appears in committed_delta.fact_predicates. Return [] for anything else. Never return texts from other scenes or other turns (a copied future secret must not be excusable).
3. `attributeNarration(narration, eligible)` -> array of spans in order covering the WHOLE narration string: {text, origin:'authored'|'narrator', source?}. A span is 'authored' only if an eligible text occurs in the narration as a literal substring after normalizing whitespace runs and curly versus straight quotes/apostrophes (normalize both sides identically; map offsets back so span texts are the original substrings). Everything else is 'narrator'. If two eligible texts overlap, keep the longer. A narrator-modified version of an authored sentence therefore stays 'narrator' (conservative: no exemption). Never lose or reorder characters: concatenating span texts reproduces the narration exactly (assert this in tests).
4. `knowledgeAvailableByTurn(turnsWithBundles)` -> for turns given in order as [{turn, bundle}], an array of {turn, available:[sorted knowledge ids committed up to AND including that turn]} using only committed bundles' selected_reveal.knowledge_ids. (Temporal eligibility: a fact earned later must not excuse an earlier turn.)

ALSO a read-only audit tool frontend/e2e/attribution-audit.js (CLI: `node e2e/attribution-audit.js <blind-player-dir> [out.json]`, importable function `auditAttribution(dir)`): <dir> holds saved files like e2e-blind-player-r1.json (replicates->scenes->turns with turn, text, rejected) and e2e-blind-player-bundles-r1.json (replicates->scenes->bundles:[{turn, attempt_bundle}]); join bundles to turns by scene and turn number. For every committed turn report: scene, turn, eligible texts (count and source kinds), authored spans found (count, chars), narrator chars, and `eligible_unmatched` (eligible texts that did NOT appear literally in the turn text: the narrator may have rewritten or dropped them). Print/return totals: turns audited, turns with any eligible text, eligible texts found vs not found by kind, fraction of narration characters attributed authored, and the list of turns whose bundle says transition_cause forced/timer or story_complete but where NO authored span was found (suspicious: attribution gap). Skip turns with no bundle (count them). A real directory to try (read-only) is /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/keep/canonical-x3/ -- run the CLI on it once and put the printed totals in your notes; also run it on /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/keep/raw-x3/ if it exists. Do not copy those files into the repo.

TESTS (node:test, hermetic; use small synthetic authored/bundle objects plus one test against the REAL package via loadAuthoredText that checks structural facts without pinning counts, e.g. the 3B->3C bridge text contains 'began the broadcast' and is reachable through the `3B>3C` key): eligibility per kind and per outcome (rejected/game_break/operational_failure -> []), no cross-scene texts, curly-quote normalization, overlap handling, exact reconstruction, narrator-modified sentence stays narrator, knowledgeAvailableByTurn temporal order, audit on a tiny synthetic directory written to a temp dir (including a turn with no bundle and a forced turn with no span).

HOW TO RUN: from the worktree `ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/frontend/node_modules frontend/node_modules` if missing (gitignored), then `cd frontend && node --test e2e/authored-spans.test.js e2e/attribution-audit.test.js e2e/authored-delivery.test.js e2e/judge-journeys.test.js` and `node --check` each new .js. Match surrounding style and comment density. Notes (the eligibility rules you chose and why, audit totals on the two real directories, any texts the engine can append that you could not attribute) to /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/stage2-notes/spans-notes.md.
